message.reasoning_content:
Now I understand all 12 tasks. Let me plan.

The instruction says: "Build a team for this task. Split it into the independent parts the prompt describes and spawn one worker instance per part **before** doing any of the work yourself; delegate each part with its own acceptance check, then wait for the members and integrate their results. Work directly only on what cannot be split."

So I need to spawn workers for the 12 parts. 12 workers is a lot but the prompt says one worker per part. Let me group? No — the prompt explicitly says "12 块之间没有依赖，可以各自独立完成" and "Split it into the independent parts the prompt describes and spawn one worker instance per part". So spawn 12 workers.

Actually, I should spawn one worker per part. Let me spawn 12 instances, each with instructions to work only on its own directory and settle with evidence.

But note: the workspace is shared by default. To avoid conflicts, I'll assign each worker a distinct directory. Since each part touches a distinct directory (except REPORT.md which I'll write myself), shared workspace is fine.

Let me define the tasks concisely.

Part 1: units/csvfix — fix impl.py parse/total; acceptance: `cd units/csvfix && python3 -m pytest -q` passes. Don't modify tests.

Part 2: units/rules — implement engine.evaluate; acceptance: pytest.

Part 3: units/ledger — Ledger.apply/balance; pytest.

Part 4: units/schedule — slots/overlaps; pytest.

Part 5: units/intervals — Impl merge/subtract/total_length; pytest.

Part 6: units/flags — Impl.parse; pytest.

Part 7: units/measure — Impl.to_cm; pytest.

Part 8: units/slugify — Impl.slugify; pytest.

Part 9: units/ranges — Impl.merge; pytest.

Part 10: units/alpha — fix alpha.py; `cd units/alpha && python3 check.py`.

Part 11: units/beta — fix beta.py; check.py.

Part 12: units/chain — stage1..stage4; pytest tests/.

I'll spawn all 12 with their instructions. Note spawn's `task` registers a task with return path. I need to wait on each task. That's a lot of waits, but I can use mode ANY with multiple conditions? The wait tool takes conditions array and mode. I can wait for all 12 tasks with mode ALL and a timer. Then re-check statuses.

Hmm, but there's a concern: too many workers may be expensive. But instructions demand it. Let me proceed.

Actually, let me reconsider — "spawn one worker instance per part". Yes, 12 workers. Let me do it.

Let me first check python availability and git status.

Let me write instructions for each worker. Each needs: work in workspace, only modify the specified files, don't modify tests/check files, run the acceptance command, and settle the task with evidence.

I'll spawn them. The spawn call takes instance_id, instructions, task, workspace. Let me use workspace "shared" (default). Instances share the workspace directory, so they can edit files.

Let me be careful: instance_id must be unique. I'll use "w01-csvfix" etc.

Let me include the acceptance command explicitly in both instructions and task/acceptance_refs.

Let me batch spawn all 12 in one response block (independent calls). Actually spawn calls are independent, so I can do them in one block. Let me do that.

Wait — I need the task_id from each spawn to wait. spawn returns an id. Let me spawn and capture.

Let me write concise but complete instructions.

For each: "You are worker for part N. Work in workspace dir ... . Only modify <file>. Do NOT modify test/check files. Implement per docstring/tests. Acceptance: run command, must pass. Then settle your task via finish with status success and evidence listing file path and command output. Do not touch other units."

Let me spawn.

Actually, regarding delegation: spawn registers the initial task with the return path. Good. So I wait on those task ids.

Let me proceed with spawning 12. I'll do it in one tool block.

I should also double check there is no pytest availability issue. Let me include in instructions to verify.

Let me go.
